title: Agent and app management: who can use which Teams app or agent?
summary: The page is held because it says built-in agent availability has no documented automation, although the Facilitator setup guidance explicitly points to app centric management, whose documentation provides PowerShell automation. The Channel Agent setup page also gives a conflicting management route that should be disclosed alongside the already reported Facilitator discrepancy.

claims.claim: App availability is configured in Teams admin center through Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability > Available to.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. Select Edit availability. Select the required option from Available to menu.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups -OperationType Add -Groups <group-ids> assigns app availability to groups.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block controls an app's organisation-wide status.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked $true is a documented app-state operation, with its direction explicitly treated as ambiguous on this page.
claims.quote:
PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings are reached through Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings.
claims.quote: On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. You can then configure the settings in the pane.

claims.claim: An automation call mapped to the org-wide default-availability control is not established in Microsoft documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Org-wide app settings PowerShell Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings GlobalApp DefaultApp PrivateApp mapping; Org-wide app settings Graph PowerShell. Read manage-apps, app-centric-management and update-m365unifiedtenantsettings; no default-availability mapping.

claims.claim: Built-in agent availability is configured through Teams admin center > Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents > agent > Edit availability.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and go to Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents. To change who can use an agent, select one or more agents and choose Edit availability.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents only admin-centre routes, and no PowerShell or API call, for changing built-in Teams agent availability.
claims.quote: You can also use app centric management to allow and block, create policies, and assign users.
claims.fix: Set controls[3].api to powershell, call 'Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups -OperationType Add -Groups <group-ids>', docs https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/update-m365teamsapp. Add to its note: 'The Facilitator setup page documents app centric management for assigning users, whose reference documents this PowerShell operation; the Manage apps overview instead directs built-in agents to the dedicated page.' The applicability source is https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/facilitator-teams and the automation source is https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management. Replace the last Open questions item with 'Is there a PowerShell or API call to move a tenant to unified app management? Microsoft documents only the admin centre route.'

claims.claim: The unified-management move is initiated through Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Move to unified app management.
claims.quote: Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. Select Move to unified app management. A dialog box appears to ask for your consent to move to the unified agent and app management experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a PowerShell or API operation to move a tenant to unified agent and app management.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams move to unified app management migration consent PowerShell API. Read uam-tac-mac and update-m365unifiedtenantsettings; search results describe UI consent and app-assignment automation, not an operation that unifies the tenant.

claims.claim: An agent is blocked through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft documents the Teams Administrator role for using the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Availability changes take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect.

claims.claim: AppAssignmentType accepts Everyone.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone

claims.claim: AppAssignmentType accepts Noone.
claims.quote:
-AppAssignmentType
App availability type.
Parameter sets
(Everyone
UsersandGroups
Noone)

claims.claim: Guests cannot use an app set to Specific users or groups, even when assigned to it.
claims.quote: Guests can't use the app if this option is selected and even if guests are assigned to the app.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes its -IsBlocked $true examples as unblocking.
claims.quote:
PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings documents a GlobalApp setting.
claims.quote:
Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings -SettingName GlobalApp -SettingValue None
Updates the tenant setting for GlobalApp to None

claims.claim: Built-in agents can be made available to everyone, specific users or groups, or no one.
claims.quote: You can make an agent available to everyone, to specific users or groups, or to no one.

claims.claim: The Microsoft apps org-wide setting no longer governs built-in Teams agents.
claims.quote: These agents are no longer controlled by the Microsoft apps setting. You now manage them from the dedicated Built-in Teams agents page in the Teams admin center.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Only a Global admin can consent to and apply the final unified-management move.
claims.quote: Only a Global admin can give consent and apply the final changes.

claims.where: controls[4].note; What it is: Unified management
claims.claim: Tenants that never modified org-wide defaults, availability or app blocking settings in either admin centre are unified automatically.
claims.quote: If your tenant never modified its org-wide defaults, app availability, or app block or unblock settings in either TAC or MAC, then your tenant's app availability policies are automatically unified.

claims.claim: The package-block API is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change.

claims.claim: The package-block API needs delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Cost and licensing: Agent package API
claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Teams admin center provides controls for allowing and blocking Teams apps and agents.
claims.quote: As an admin, you control access to all types of agents and apps that are used across your organization. Teams provides granular controls to configure access for each agent and app and for each user.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: App centric management sets access per app for individual users or groups.
claims.quote: This functionality lets you specify which users and groups can use each app or a copilot agent and you can control it on a per-app basis.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Administrators can set default availability for newly published apps.
claims.quote: In addition to defining the availability of an app, you can also control the default app availability of any new apps. You can control it for each type of app.

claims.claim: Each app has three availability types: Everyone, Specific users or groups, and No one.
claims.quote:
When using this functionality, you determine access to apps using one of the following options for each app:
Everyone
Specific users or groups
No one

claims.claim: Microsoft calls the per-app access mechanism app centric management.
claims.quote: App centric management feature simplifies these settings. Each app contains its access definition using a list of users and groups that you assign to it.

claims.claim: App centric management replaces app permission policies.
claims.quote: Use the feature if already auto-migrated or manually migrate to app centric management. It replaces app permission policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes the previous App permission policies as deprecated.
claims.quote: The previous App permission policies is deprecated.

claims.where: What it is: settings table; What to check
claims.claim: Org-wide app settings provide defaults by Microsoft, third-party and custom app type.
claims.quote: Under Microsoft apps, a single control automatically enables users to install and use any available agents and apps by default. Under Third-party apps, a single control manages the bulk availability of both the new and existing third-party agents and apps.

claims.where: What it is: settings table; Governance controls
claims.claim: Allow or Block determines an individual app's organisation-wide usability.
claims.quote: You can allow or block specific agents and apps on either the Manage apps page or in the app details page.

claims.claim: Availability determines which users and groups may use the app.
claims.quote: Specific users or groups | Only the users and groups that you select can use the app.

claims.where: What it is: after settings table
claims.claim: Microsoft says the applicable access settings must allow an app for it to be allowed.
claims.quote: To allow an agent or app, you must do all of the following settings.

claims.where: What it is: after settings table
claims.claim: Microsoft says any one of the applicable access controls can block an app.
claims.quote: To block an agent or app, use any one of the following settings:

claims.where: summary; What it is: Unified management
claims.claim: After unification, changes to org-wide settings, app status and availability synchronise in both directions between Teams and Microsoft 365 admin centres.
claims.quote: After your tenant is unified, all changes to org-wide settings, agent app, status, or availability in TAC are automatically synchronized in MAC and vice versa.

claims.claim: Unified management governs app availability across Teams, Outlook and Microsoft Copilot apps.
claims.quote: Ensures org-wide defaults for both admin centers are in sync and governs app availability across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft Copilot apps

claims.claim: Tenants with modified settings can opt into unification through the Manage apps guided experience.
claims.quote: If your tenant's org-wide default settings, app availability, or app block and unblock settings in either TAC or MAC are previously modified, then you can unify your tenant's agent or app settings

claims.where: What it is: Built-in Teams agents; What to check
claims.claim: Channel Agent, Facilitator and other built-in Teams agents are managed on Built-in Teams agents, not Manage apps.
claims.quote: Built-in Teams agents like Channel Agent, Facilitator, and other built-in agents available across chats, channels, and meetings are managed from the Built-In Teams agents page, not the Manage apps page.
claims.fix: After the Facilitator route discrepancy, add: 'The Channel Agent setup page likewise directs administrators to Teams apps > Manage apps > Channel Agent > Allow or Block.' Cite and add to sources https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/set-up-channel-agent-teams, titled 'Set up a Channel Agent for Microsoft Teams'. Its documented steps select Teams apps > Manage apps, select Channel Agent, and select Allow or Block in the Actions menu.

claims.where: What it is: Built-in Teams agents
claims.claim: The Facilitator setup page still gives Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block, differing from the overview's dedicated built-in-agent route.
claims.quote: In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps. In the apps list's search box, search for Facilitator. Select Facilitator from the app list. In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.claim: For new organisations, Microsoft documents a default that lets users install apps.
claims.quote: For new organizations, the default setting is set to let users install apps by default.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits; Governance controls
claims.claim: Org-wide settings apply to new store apps and existing apps whose availability was not actively changed.
claims.quote:
The Org-wide app settings apply to:
All the new apps made available in Teams app store.
All the existing apps that you didn't actively manage, that is, you didn't change the availability of.

claims.claim: The Manage apps, app centric management and unified-management pages publish no licence for the management settings themselves.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams app centric management unified app management admin settings license pricing meter. Read manage-apps, app-centric-management and uam-tac-mac in full; product and app licensing references do not specify a licence or meter for these management settings.

claims.claim: Except for anonymously joining meetings, each organisation user needs a Teams licence to use Teams.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Paid third-party apps
claims.claim: Licences for services offered by third-party apps can be purchased from Manage apps.
claims.quote: You can purchase licenses for services offered by third-party apps from the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Paid third-party apps
claims.claim: The documented app-purchase payment methods include credit card, debit card and invoice billing.
claims.quote: You can purchase apps using a credit card, debit card, or with invoice billing.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Paid third-party apps
claims.claim: Plans and pricing are shown on the app details page in Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Select Purchase on the Manage apps page to open the Plans and pricing tab on the app details page. You can review the plans and pricing information available in admin center.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Paid third-party apps
claims.claim: Invoice billing requires an admin account with Teams Administrator and Billing Administrator roles.
claims.quote: Invoice billing is only available for an admin account that has Teams Administrator and Billing Administrator role.

claims.claim: Show tailored apps applies to users with an F licence.
claims.quote: Under Tailored apps, turn off or turn on Show tailored apps. When this setting is on, users with an F license get the tailored frontline agent and app experience.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Availability changes can exceptionally take up to six days to appear in the client.
claims.quote: In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Migration is one-way
claims.claim: After switching to app centric management, permission policies cannot be accessed, edited or used.
claims.quote: After you switch to this feature, you can't access, edit, or use permission policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Migration is one-way
claims.claim: App centric management migration cannot be reverted.
claims.quote: Once your organization migrates, you can't revert the migration.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Org-wide settings skip managed apps; Governance controls
claims.claim: Saved individual availability assignments override org-wide defaults and remain intact when the third-party setting changes.
claims.quote:
The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to:
All apps that have user assignment set to Specific users and groups and saved by you.
All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually.
Any blocked apps.

claims.claim: Everyone includes guests.
claims.quote: Everyone | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Conflicting policies on auto-migration
claims.claim: One description says a globally allowed app blocked in a custom policy becomes available to all tenant users, except none for EDU customers.
claims.quote: Here, the app is available to all users of the tenant, except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Conflicting policies on auto-migration
claims.claim: The same page's auto-migration process section describes the conflict outcome as allowing the affected user rather than explicitly giving the all-users and EDU outcomes.
claims.quote: Microsoft auto-migrates the app as allowed for that user. During the auto migration, one security group is created for each custom app permission policy.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Two admin centres out of step
claims.claim: Before unification, Microsoft advises keeping blocked-app and org-wide settings synchronised in both admin centres.
claims.quote: Until your tenant is migrated to unified app management, ensure that the settings in both admin centers, such as blocked apps or org-wide app settings, remain synchronized.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Two admin centres out of step
claims.claim: Before unification, blocking a cross-application app in Integrated apps affects Outlook and the Microsoft Copilot application, not Teams.
claims.quote: The app is only be blocked in the Microsoft Copilot application and Outlook. Teams continues to honor the current setting for Teams Apps made in the Teams admin center

claims.where: Risks and limits: Bulk edits need PowerShell
claims.claim: Teams admin center cannot update app availability in bulk, whereas PowerShell can.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Bulk edits need PowerShell
claims.claim: Up to 99 users or groups can be added to an app at a time.
claims.quote: You can add up to 99 users or groups at a time to an app.

claims.claim: Administrators can only view and manage apps deployed in their tenant's release channel.
claims.quote: You can only view and manage agents and apps that are deployed in the same release channel as your tenant is.

claims.claim: Third-party agents and apps are blocked by default in GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: In a Microsoft 365 Government - GCC, GCCH and DoD deployment of Teams, all third-party agents and apps are blocked by default.

claims.claim: Enabling app purchasing also enables in-app purchasing.
claims.quote: When you enable app purchasing, it also turns on in-app purchasing.

claims.claim: Blocking an app prevents users making in-app purchases in it.
claims.quote: To prevent users from making in-app purchases, you can block the app.

claims.claim: Any Teams or Global admin can prepare unified-management changes up to the Review summary page.
claims.quote: Any Teams or Global admin can make updates upto the Review summary page.

claims.claim: The documented Microsoft 365 Integrated apps controls are available to Global Administrators.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents disabling third-party app purchases with the MSCommerce PowerShell module.
claims.quote: To prevent users from purchasing third-party apps, you can disable purchases using the MSCommerce PowerShell module.

claims.claim: Usage reports offers a Teams app usage report.
claims.quote: The Teams agent and app usage report provides information about which agents and apps in use, active users, and other usage information. | Usage reports | Teams app usage report

claims.claim: Teams admin center can export the app catalogue as CSV.
claims.quote:
Export agent and app catalog as CSV
As an admin, you can export the entire agent and app catalog for your org from the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Get-AllM365TeamsApps returns the app catalogue with status information.
claims.quote: Get-AllM365TeamsApps retrieves a complete list of all Teams apps in an organization, their statuses, and their availability information.

claims.claim: Get-AllM365TeamsApps returns app availability information.
claims.quote:
AvailableTo Provides available to properties for the app. Properties:
AssignmentType: App availability type. Values:
Everyone
UsersandGroups
Noone

claims.claim: Get-AllM365TeamsApps identifies the user who last updated app availability.
claims.quote: AssignedBy: UserID of the last user who updated the app available to value.

-IsBlocked

claims.quote: Searched: Teams Org-wide app settings PowerShell Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings GlobalApp DefaultApp PrivateApp mapping. Read update-m365unifiedtenantsettings in full: names, values and examples are given, but no UI mapping.

claims.claim: The auto-migration process description creates one security group per custom app permission policy.
claims.quote: During the auto migration, one security group is created for each custom app permission policy.

claims.where: What it is: settings table; What to check
claims.claim: Org-wide app settings include a control for default installation and use of available custom apps.
claims.quote: Under Custom apps, turn off or turn on Let users install and use available apps by default option. This setting controls whether users can install and use the custom agents and apps that you make available to them.

claims.claim: The Manage apps, app centric management and unified-management pages publish no meter for these management settings themselves.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams app centric management unified app management admin settings license pricing meter. Read manage-apps, app-centric-management and uam-tac-mac in full; no meter for the management settings themselves is stated.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center agent-blocking control blocks access across the organisation.
claims.quote: Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
